validity.recommendation: No change needed to existence, classification, length, capacity, construction year, delay flag, cost, or endpoints.
validity.researcher_notes: Existence and classification independently confirmed, in both English and Russian sources. Line D is real, ongoing (if long-stalled) infrastructure: intergovernmental agreement Sept 2013, CNPC/Trans-Asia + Tajiktransgaz JV formed and foundation ceremony held 13 Sep 2014 (Xi Jinping + Rahmon in attendance), Tajik-section tunneling (42 tunnels, 63.3 km) documented as ongoing through at least 2020-2023, and the project remains an active diplomatic topic through mid-2026. Correctly classified as a gas transmission trunk (not gathering/feeder) -- it is explicitly the fourth parallel trunk of the Central Asia-China Gas Pipeline system, alongside Lines A/B/C. Route/endpoints confirmed: origin Galkynysh gas field, Turkmenistan; transits Uzbekistan (205 km), Tajikistan (391 km), Kyrgyzstan (215 km); enters China near Irkeshtam and terminates at Wuqia county, Xinjiang (confirmed as the planned first Chinese receiving point in two independent trade-press sources) -- this is the same Wuqia that anchors the domestic West-East Gas Pipeline 4. Length 966.00 km confirmed at two-decimal-equivalent precision by Tajikistan's own Ministry of Energy and Water Resources page (391 km Tajik section) and independently by a Russian oil/gas trade outlet giving the full five-country breakdown (Uzbekistan 205 + Tajikistan 391 + Kyrgyzstan 215 + China 155 = 966, Turkmenistan section the balance) -- two independent sources, exact match, no rounding conflict. Capacity 30.00 bcm/y confirmed repeatedly (would raise total CAGP network capacity 55->85 bcm/y once operational) -- high tier, >=2 independent. ConstructionYear 2014 confirmed via the Sept 13, 2014 foundation ceremony, reported independently by multiple outlets. Delayed=yes/DelayType=confirmed is well supported: Tajikistan's Energy Minister explicitly attributed the hold-up to unresolved gas-pricing disagreements among the other participating countries (Tajikistan's own section is complete on its telling), and coverage as recent as June 2026 still describes Line D as 'yet to be implemented.' SegmentCost $6.70bn confirmed verbatim ('Estimated in 2014 to cost US$6.7 billion') in a trade-press republication of the underlying Reuters reporting -- note GEM's own wiki page paraphrases the same Reuters piece as '$6.5 billion' elsewhere, but the actual article text reads $6.7 billion, matching the sheet exactly; treat as one Reuters-origin figure, not two disagreeing sources. FuelSource=Galkynysh gas field confirmed independently of the sheet's own (currently 403'd) S&P Global ref by the Tajik ministry page, the Reuters-derived cost article, and the CNPC/Tajiktransgaz JV background piece -- the existing FuelSource ref (S&P Global) returned HTTP 403 (blocked, not deleted) so it should be KEPT per the access-failure rule, not dropped.

validity.recommendation: Correct Owner2/Owner3: replace 'Turkmengaz' and 'QazaqGaz' with 'Tajiktransgaz' (the confirmed 50% co-owner of the operating JV alongside Owner1). Turkmengaz and QazaqGaz are not corroborated as owners of Line D by any independent source found; recommend Update investigate and fix, not applied here.
validity.researcher_notes: Two independent sources (AidData's project financing record and an Enerdata daily-news item on the original 2014 JV agreement) agree that the Tajikistan-section operating company -- which the sheet's own Operator field names, 'Trans-Tajik Gas Pipeline Co Ltd' (TTGP) -- is a 50/50 joint venture between (1) Trans-Asia Gas Pipeline Company Limited, a CNPC subsidiary (= the sheet's Owner1, confirmed correct), and (2) OJSC Tajiktransgaz, Tajikistan's state gas-transport company. Neither source names Turkmengaz or QazaqGaz as an owner of this JV or of Line D at all -- Tajiktransgaz, the actual second owner, is entirely absent from the sheet's Owner columns. QazaqGaz in particular is geographically implausible here: Line D was purpose-built to bypass Kazakhstan, routing Turkmenistan->Uzbekistan->Tajikistan->Kyrgyzstan->China specifically to avoid Kazakh transit dependency (the whole point of the new route versus Lines A/B/C). Independent search confirms QazaqGaz's only documented CAGP role is via the 'Turkmenistan-Uzbekistan-Kazakhstan-China' pipeline coordinating committee -- i.e. Lines A/B/C, a different route that does cross Kazakhstan, not Line D. GEM's own wiki page for this pipeline (read for leads only, not cited) independently lists Line D's owners as 'Trans-Tajik Gas Pipeline Company Ltd and Tajiktransgaz' -- consistent with the independent sourcing above and inconsistent with the sheet's own Owner2/Owner3 values, suggesting an internal GEM data inconsistency between the wiki narrative and the operators/owners tab, not just a sourcing gap. Turkmengaz is Turkmenistan's state gas producer/Galkynysh-field operator (the FuelSource, correctly) but no source found ties it to pipeline ownership of Line D specifically.

validity.recommendation: Flag StartYear1=2022 as unsupported; no source found corroborates 2022 as a target/actual start date. Recommend Update review and either source a current target date or blank the field rather than carry an apparently stale figure -- not changed here (no fabricated ref).
validity.researcher_notes: The sheet's StartYear1 value (2022) has no independent corroboration in anything found -- and contemporary reporting instead points the other way: the project's original CNPC-era target was completion by end-2020/January 2020 for all four lines, and by around 2021 outlets were reporting 'no completion date has been set.' As of June 2026 the pipeline is still described as unrealized, with construction resumption contingent on an unresolved Turkmenistan-China gas price agreement. No source names 2022 specifically as any kind of target, milestone, or actual event date for Line D. This is left UNRESOLVED (see fills) rather than corrected, since I found no sourced replacement value either -- only that 2022 itself appears to be an unsupported/stale figure.

status_reviews.researcher_notes: Searched Russian- and English-language coverage through the current date (Aug 2026) for any sign of actual construction resumption or completion. Found none. A mid-2026 (22 Jun 2026) Russian-language survey of Turkmenistan's oil/gas sector states plainly that the 'long-discussed fourth pipeline branch (line D) remains yet to be implemented,' despite covering major concurrent Turkmenistan-CNPC and Turkmenistan-Petronas developments in the same piece -- i.e. this is a considered, current statement, not an old fact being repeated. A January 2026 Russian-language roundup notes Turkmengaz stated the Galkynysh field's fourth development phase (beginning early 2026) would 'include completion of Line D,' and that CNPC 'plans to launch Line D... to increase imports to 65 bcm/y' -- but frames this explicitly as a repeatedly-deferred promise ('the long-suffering Line D branch was promised to launch several years ago, but implementation is dragging on'), not a report of actual pipe-laying resuming. An April 2026 Turkmengaz-CNPC contract for Galkynysh phase-4 field development ($5.1bn per Turkmengaz's own chairman) is upstream gas-field investment, not pipeline construction, and no source connects it to Line D groundbreaking. Tajikistan's Energy Minister (via qazinform, undated but referencing ongoing conditions) continues to attribute the hold-up to unresolved inter-country gas pricing, with Tajikistan's own section already complete on its telling. Net: sustained, current (through mid-2026) independent coverage exists and it is unanimous that Line D has NOT resumed physical construction or restarted -- this is an actively-covered stalled project, not a story that has gone quiet, so 'stale'/dormancy-inference does not apply (that rule is for the absence of independent news, not for news that confirms continued non-progress). 'shelved' remains the accurate status; no change proposed.

fills.researcher_notes: Tajikistan's Energy Minister explicitly names ongoing inter-country gas-pricing disagreement as the delay cause (qazinform); a June 2026 independent piece confirms the branch is still 'yet to be implemented' despite a decade-plus of promises. Two independent sources, both current.

Verbatim match: 'Estimated in 2014 to cost US$6.7 billion, Line D would carry 30 billion m3/yr of gas.' This traces to the same underlying 2023 Reuters wire story that is republished (with the same figure) across several other outlets (Business Recorder, Nasdaq, Tribune, Zawya) -- one origin, not independently corroborated, so tier=medium/independent=false per the wire-story rule. No second, differently-sourced figure found; GEM's own wiki page paraphrases the same Reuters piece elsewhere as '$6.5 billion,' which is a paraphrase mismatch against the actual article text ($6.7bn, matching the sheet), not a second independent estimate.

AidData's detailed financing record names 'Trans-Tajik Gas Pipeline Company Limited (TTGP)' explicitly as the joint venture managing financing, construction, and operation of the Tajikistan section. Enerdata's contemporaneous (2014) report independently corroborates the underlying JV structure (CNPC subsidiary Trans-Asia Gas Pipeline Company + Tajiktransgaz) but does not use the exact legal name 'Trans-Tajik Gas Pipeline Co Ltd,' so I'm citing AidData alone for the literal Operator string (tier=medium) while noting the JV's existence is independently corroborated (see the Owner concern above, tier=high).

Not sourcing this as-is: Owner1 (Trans-Asia Gas Pipeline Co Ltd) is independently confirmed correct, but Owner2 (Turkmengaz) and Owner3 (QazaqGaz) are not corroborated by any source found -- see the attribution concern above, which recommends Owner2 be corrected to Tajiktransgaz instead. Left UNRESOLVED rather than citing a ref that would appear to validate the current Owner2/Owner3 values, per the no-auto-apply / concern-first rule.

No source found supports 2022 as any kind of start/completion date for Line D -- see the spec concern above. The project's original (now long-abandoned) CNPC-era target was end-2020/Jan-2020, and by ~2021 reporting already said no completion date had been set; nothing found ties 2022 specifically to this pipeline. Left UNRESOLVED rather than fabricate or guess a replacement date; recommend Update decide whether to blank the field pending a genuinely sourced target.

summary: P2030 (CAGP Line D) confirmed real, correctly classified, and not a duplicate of any in-scope roster row; length/capacity/construction-year/cost/delay-status/endpoints all independently corroborated (2+ sources) and status='shelved' reconfirmed current through Jun 2026. Two concerns staged: an attribution finding (Owner2/Owner3 'Turkmengaz'/'QazaqGaz' uncorroborated -- true second owner is Tajiktransgaz, confirmed by 2 independent sources; QazaqGaz's real CAGP role is on the Kazakhstan-transit Lines A/B/C route Line D was built to bypass) and a spec finding (StartYear1=2022 unsupported by any source). 2 fills UNRESOLVED (Owner, StartYear1) rather than sourcing values I believe are wrong.
